maya: heads up — autotuner chose kernel-llr4 for the seqlen=1024 hotpath on prod-A100, and with continuous batching on we see ~+15% p95 vs the previous kernel. repro below.
kevin: can you paste the perf numbers and request distribution? which model/quant/state?
maya: model=redwood-13b-q4_0, quant=q4_0, batch distribution is very skewed (70% small, 20% mid, 10% long). baseline (kernel-oldpath) p95=78ms, new k-llr4 p95=90ms, mean change +12%. simple log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T18:12:02Z] route=seqlen-1024 kernel=kernel-llr4 p95=90ms p50=28ms gpu=A100
[2026-03-15T18:12:02Z] route=seqlen-1024 kernel=kernel-oldpath p95=78ms p50=26ms gpu=A100
```
kevin: hmm autotuner should be arch-aware; did it mis-detect hardware family or profile window was noisy?
lia: @maya can you run bench/kernel_probe.py with CONT_BATCH=1 and the same seqlen histogram? bench-bot can aggregate.
bench-bot: queued run id=bb-778, running on pool/ci-small. will post microbench results.
bench-bot: results: kernel-oldpath p95=76ms, kernel-llr4 p95=89ms, launch-overhead delta ~+6ms when cont-batching enabled. (script: `bench/kernel_probe.py --model redwood-13b-q4_0 --hist=prod-hist.json --cont-batch`)
oscar: that launch delta smells like a kernel start-up path that doesn't amortize under our continuous-batching scheduler. maybe kernel-llr4 has larger module init or different cuLaunch config.
sara: also check KV cache footprint: llr4 uses a different KV packing that increases persistent memory per-request which can change CUDA kernel occupancy and also increase host->device prep time.
maya: good point — KV warmup traces show extra memcpy at tail. small trace:
```
[perf] memcpy_h2d size=1.2MB time=3.8ms (old) vs 6.9ms (llr4)
[perf] kernel_launch overhead  +5.9ms avg on cont-batch flows
```
oscar: temporary mitigation: add a guard in the autotuner that disables kernel-llr4 when continuous_batching=true and seq_len_mean>512. simple toggle in runtime config.
kevin: propose autotuner change: require >=2x throughput improvement or <1.02 latency regression in sampled cont-batch experiments before switching kernel for hotpath. prevents noisy flips.
lia: agree, also add a per-arch whitelist. we've seen k-llr4 benefits on Ampere for long single-request latency but regresses on our cont-batch scheduler on older kernels/drivers.
maya: i've pushed a hotfix: runtime flag `kernel.autotune.cont_batch_protect = true` and rolled back the k-llr4 for model=redwood-13b-q4_0 on prod-A100. deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: rollout started -> canary on infra-cluster-7 (5%) -> monitoring link: https://grafana/redwood/runtime/1951234567
sara: follow-up tasks: 1) nvprof traces to confirm memcpy source, 2) kernel symbol-level inspection for llr4, 3) add microbench cont-batch tests to autotuner harness.
oscar: i'll open ISSUE-452 and add a short RCA when we have nvprof output.
maya: thanks all — disabling autotune flip fixed p95 back to ~78ms on canary. will keep cont-batch microbench in the autotune job. :white_check_mark:
kevin: nice catch. lets add a note in the autotuner README about cont-batch interactions.
lia: and schedule a brief sync with ML infra next week to review kernel heuristics.
maya: o/"
